subject: physical-education
unitTitle: Access, Cost, Facilities, and Community Resources
title: Guided practice B: building an activity life on a small budget
focus: building an activity life on a small budget
essentialQuestion: What does it actually cost to stay active, and what costs nothing?
materials: publicly available facility and program information
privacySafeScenario: Produce an access plan comparing at least three ways to stay active after graduation on different budgets, including one that costs nothing, and identify the failure point of each.
studentTask: Learner applies building an activity life on a small budget in a new situation at a self-set intensity and records what they did, noticed, and would adjust.
knowledgeCheck: In one concise response, explain the key idea behind building an activity life on a small budget and name one adjustment for the next session.
completionCriteria: The learner completes or fully describes the building an activity life on a small budget task using a version their body and setting allow.
The learner gives a cue, principle, tactic, or documented process rather than an unexplained result.
The learner self-assesses against the stated criteria and identifies one next adjustment.
adaptationChoices: The comparison may be written, tabled, or spoken; publicly available information is supplied if the learner cannot research independently.
extensionChallenge: Apply building an activity life on a small budget under a new constraint, in a different activity, or teach the cue to someone else — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.
The comparison may be written, tabled, or spoken; publicly available information is supplied if the learner cannot research independently.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to notice or try one safe, optional example of building an activity life on a small budget in daily life. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or public performance is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
